subject: Data sojourns, cross-border handling and tombstone deletion — Q&A
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@clearline.health>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial questions — where requests are processed and how long they persist

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the demo last week — Clearline is evaluating Redwood for several PII-heavy inference flows. Before we loop procurement I need a concise picture of two things for our security team:

1) Where inference requests and transient state are executed (regions and any third-party subprocessors that touch payloads). Is EU traffic ever routed through US-hosted nodes or vendor hops?
2) Retention / deletion behavior — specifically the maximum time any customer payload (including prefixes, KV cache entries, and logs) could persist after a request completes. We need a description we can include in our vendor risk register.

If you have a short evidence pack or CSV of subprocessors that would be ideal.

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement is waiting on the security review.

Best,
Alex
CTO, Clearline Health

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex@clearline.health>
Date: 2026-10-15T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions — where requests are processed and how long they persist
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>

Hi Alex — great to hear you and the team found the demo useful. Short answers below and I'm attaching a one-page evidence summary plus our latest subprocessor inventory. More detail and logs evidence are available if you want a walkthrough.

1) Execution locales:
- Requests are executed in the region you select on the model endpoint. For Clearline we can pin to the EU (Frankfurt) or US (us-west-2). By default EU-resident endpoints keep execution and ephemeral caches in-region.
- Smart routing may fall back to alternate regions only under capacity emergencies; we provide explicit policy controls (region pin + failover deny) for regulated customers.
- Subprocessors: our runtime uses (a) cloud provider managed VPS/GPU infra, (b) managed logging (retention controls), and (c) a third-party telemetry agent for health metrics. The attached CSV lists provider names and contract roles for Q3.

2) Retention and deletion:
- Persistent customer artifacts: model inputs/results are not persisted in long-term storage unless you enable logging. If logging is enabled we retain logs for the configurable retention window (default 30 days).
- Ephemeral caches (KV/prefix caches): these are in-memory by default and flushed on instance termination; we do snapshot fallback only for warm-start efficiency — snapshots are encrypted at rest and removed within 24 hours of instance teardown by default.
- Tombstone policy: when you request data deletion, we run a queued delete job: in-region shards and object stores are cleared within 72 hours; indexing/backup scrubs complete within 30 days.

Attachments: redwood-residency-evidence-summary.pdf, subprocessor-inventory-2026Q3.csv (see attached)

I can loop in our security lead for any deeper technical evidence. Want me to add Karthik and Jordan to provide the low-level cache/ops details?

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai

Hi Alex — thanks for the follow-ups and for the clear asks. Below is consolidated, vendor-ready language you can paste into your questionnaire. Attached is a single PDF combining the evidence summary, subprocessor CSV, and a short ops runbook for audit queries.

Vendor-ready consolidated answers (copyable):

A) Execution and cross-border handling
- Redwood executes inference within the region you configure for the endpoint. For EU-resident endpoints we operate compute and in-memory caches within the selected EU region (Frankfurt by default).
- Cross-region routing occurs only under explicit failover or capacity-exhaustion conditions. For regulated workloads we recommend "region pin + failover deny" which prevents automatic cross-border routing.
- Subprocessors that may touch in-flight payloads are listed in our Subprocessor Inventory (attached). All subprocessors have SOC2 or equivalent attestations recorded in our vendor dossier.

B) KV/prefix cache and persistence
- KV and prefix caches are in-memory by default and are not written to external object stores during normal serving.
- For warm-start optimization we may take encrypted snapshots to block storage; these snapshots exist only transiently and are removed on instance termination. Default snapshot lifetime is <= 24 hours; snapshots are encrypted (AES-256) and access-controlled.

C) Auditability and evidence for failover events
- All routing decisions and failover events emit an immutable audit entry (request_id, source_region, destination_region, timestamp). Customers with an enterprise contract may request an export of routing audit logs for a defined period; we provide a CSV export and a guided runbook to map request IDs to payloads where retention permits.

D) Deletion and tombstone handling
- If you instruct Redwood to delete a dataset or ask for a specific request to be purged, the deletion enters our erase workflow: object-store deletes in-region complete within 72 hours; indexing, backups, and long-tail copies are scheduled for scrub within 30 days (per our data lifecycle policy).

If you'd like, we can:
- Provide a time-limited export of recent routing audit entries for a sample window (we'll redact payloads), or
- Set up a 30-minute session with Karthik and our security team to walk through the evidence pack and run live queries.

Links/attachments included:
- Redwood residency evidence (combined PDF): https://drive.redwood.example.com/shared/CLEARLINE-RESIDENCY-EVIDENCE
- Subprocessor inventory CSV (Q3 2026)
